# reco_compliance_framework (Resource)

Manages a custom Reco compliance framework with its controls, for example to promote the same framework from a development tenant to a production tenant. Built-in frameworks cannot be managed.

The Reco API replaces a framework's controls as a whole on every update, so this resource owns the framework's controls: `controls` is the full list, and an update without `controls` removes every control (including controls added in the Reco UI). The API cannot return a framework's controls, so changes made to them outside Terraform are not detected.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "reco_posture_check" "mfa_enforced" {
  title                  = "MFA is enforced for all users"
  data_source            = "GSUITE_USERS_API"
  violation_risk_level   = "HIGH"
  violation_risk_type    = "RISK_TYPE_USER"
  conditions_jsonata     = "payload.isEnrolledIn2Sv = false"
  posture_unique_jsonata = "$.primaryEmail"
  posture_value_jsonata  = "$.primaryEmail"
}

# The controls are the framework's complete list: every apply replaces the
# controls in Reco with these, so keep all of them here.
resource "reco_compliance_framework" "internal_controls" {
  title       = "Internal Security Controls"
  description = "Our baseline security controls."
  version     = "2026.1"
  type        = "internal"

  controls = [
    {
      control_id  = "AC-1"
      title       = "Access control"
      description = "Access to systems is restricted to authorised users."
    },
    {
      control_id         = "AC-1.1"
      title              = "Multi-factor authentication"
      parent_control_id  = "AC-1"
      related_policy_ids = [reco_posture_check.mfa_enforced.id]
    },
    {
      control_id = "AC-2"
      title      = "Quarterly access review"
      manual     = true
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `title` (String) Framework display name.

### Optional

- `controls` (Attributes List) The framework's complete list of controls (at most 1000). Omitting it removes every control from the framework. The Reco API does not return this value, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected and it is empty after import. After import, add the controls to the configuration before applying any change, because applying replaces the framework's controls with the configured ones. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--controls))
- `description` (String) Longer description shown in the Reco UI.
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether the framework is active. Defaults to `false`. The Reco API only applies this when the framework is created, so changing it forces the framework to be destroyed and recreated, which also deletes its controls and changes its ID. To activate or deactivate a framework without recreating it, leave this unset and use the Reco UI; the current state is read back.
- `type` (String) Free-text framework type.
- `version` (String) Framework version string, e.g. `2024.1`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the framework was created (read-only).
- `id` (String) Compliance framework ID (UUID, set after create).
- `updated_at` (String) When the framework was last updated (read-only).

<a id="nestedatt--controls"></a>
### Nested Schema for `controls`

Required:

- `control_id` (String) Control identifier within the framework, e.g. `CC6.1`. Must be unique in the framework.

Optional:

- `description` (String) Control description.
- `manual` (Boolean) Whether the control is evaluated manually. Defaults to `false`.
- `parent_control_id` (String) `control_id` of the parent control, when this control is nested under another.
- `related_policy_ids` (Set of String) IDs of the posture checks mapped to this control (for example `reco_posture_check.example.id`). Each posture check must exist.
- `skipped` (Boolean) Whether the control is skipped. Defaults to `false`.
- `title` (String) Control display name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Import by the framework ID (the `id` in the Compliance Frameworks list).
# Only custom frameworks can be imported. The API cannot return a framework's
# controls, so add them to the configuration before applying any change:
# an apply replaces the controls in Reco with the configured ones.
import {
  to = reco_compliance_framework.internal_controls
  id = "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"
}
```
